data.prompt: Run your knapsack function on the provided test case ([1,1,1], [0,0,1], 2) and, after each inner‑loop iteration, print the current index c, the value of best[c] before the update, and the value of best[c‑w] that you use in the comparison. Record the sequence of printed lines.
data.trace_question: When you examine the printed trace, do you ever use a best[c‑w] value that was just written in the same outer‑loop iteration (i.e., after processing the same item)? Which iteration shows this, and how does it differ from the correct DP order where such a read would never happen?
data.expected_insight: The trace reveals that during the inner loop the algorithm reads best[c‑w] that was updated earlier in the same iteration for the current item, meaning a state is read before it should be written. This extra state transition is the source of the incorrect result and shows why the loop order must be topological (capacity descending).
